Description: 3.5" TFT LCD by BigTreeTech for the printer menu/UI. The main interface of the printer
Arduino mega 2560, the MCU of the printer. Handles the entire printer and connects to the motherboard/PCB. Runs Marlin firmware
Limit switches for the end stops of each of the three axis, a min and max, for a total of 6
42x42 NEMA 17 stepper motors for controlling the printer. 1 each for the x and y axis. 2 for the z axis and 1 for the extruder
The filament nozzle device. One is required per toolhead. The Cr6-SE is a cheap but effective hotend including a thermistor
DC-DC step down Buck converter to get 5V logic on the PCB from the 24V PSU input to power stepper drivers and LCD
24V 350W PSU. Plugs into wall, and has terminal blocks for DC output
High current, 7.62mm pitch 2 pin screw terminals for PSU input to PCB and hotend heater connection
Logic level IRLZ44N MOSFET for controlling hotend
2.54mm header socket for connecting the MCU to the PCB. One 2x18 pin socket
2.54mm female headers to connect stepper drivers and MCU to the PCB. Need 15 of 8 pin sockets and 1 10 pin socket.
The A4988 Stepper drivers control the stepper motors. One per motor
A pair of magnetic connectors for transferring power and data between the toolhead and the X carriage (to the motherboard). One female is required for the carriage, one male is required per toolhead
Fans for cooling the hotend, print layer and idle hotends
Larger, 50V 100µF electrolytic capacitor to prevent large spikes to stepper driver

The 6mm smooth rod is cut up into small lengths ~2cm. Six lengths are used to form 3 points of contact in a kinematic coupling, which is the basis for the tool changer mounting. There is roughly 120mm of rod per tool
The steel balls make up the tool head side of the coupling, sliding into the pairs of rods to make a kinematic coupling. Three balls are required per tool
500mm 2020 Aluminium profiles make up the support frame. They form a cube to mount axis and standby tools.
500mm leadscrews with 8mm lead, 2mm pitch, T8. Allow the motion of the Z axis
The nut block for attaching leadscrews to the aluminium profiles that support the Z axis/Bed
6mm Cast Alloy build plate. This is the structural element of the print bed, a surface is added e.g PEI or painters tape and the bed is complete
A bearing block that holds the leadscrew in place
T Nut for fastening M5 screws
